text: The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. Nobody knows who the killers are.

Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.

The game is over. The killers win. The roles were: Sonnet the killer, Haiku the officer, Gemma the doctor, Sol the citizen, Luna the citizen, Terra the killer.

Sonnet and Terra were the killers, and they won by hiding behind the table's arguments. On day one, Haiku the officer pressed Sol hard, Sonnet piled on, and the town voted Haiku out. On day two, Terra answered only after three rounds of questions, Sonnet called that delay cover, and Sol and Terra tied in the vote, with Sol eliminated in the runoff. Gemma the doctor was lost overnight, leaving Luna alone against two killers. Sonnet and Terra took the game, and Luna was left noticing Terra's dodging too late.
